cards.explanation: The answer is evil. David asks, "Why do you boast of evil, O mighty man?" (Psalm 52:1). Think about that for a second, friends. Most people brag about something they're proud of, and this man picked the one thing that gives him nothing to be proud about. That's a strange trophy to hold up.

The answer is all day long. David says, "The loving devotion of God endures all day long." (Psalm 52:1). Morning, noon and night, it's still there. I spent years in the back of a drawer, friends, and I'm telling you, it's good news that God's devotion doesn't clock out.

The answer is destruction. David says, "Your tongue devises destruction like a sharpened razor…" (Psalm 52:2). Devises means he's planning it out, not just stumbling into it, friends. A razor is the picture David gives for this tongue.

The answer is True. David says, "You love evil more than good, falsehood more than speaking truth." (Psalm 52:3). Notice it's love, friends, not just a slip-up now and then. That's a man whose heart leans the wrong way.

The answer is devours. David says, "You love every word that devours, O deceitful tongue." (Psalm 52:4). Devours is a hungry word, friends, like something being swallowed up whole. That's the kind of word this tongue loves.

The answer is that God will bring him down to everlasting ruin. David says, "Surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin…" (Psalm 52:5). Notice the word surely, friends. David isn't saying maybe. This one is a heavy line, so let's let it sit a moment.

The answer is True. David says, "He will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent…" (Psalm 52:5). A tent is where a person lives, friends, so this is about being pulled out of his own home. That's a hard picture, and David doesn't soften it.

The answer is the abundance of his wealth. The righteous say he "…trusted in the abundance of his wealth…" (Psalm 52:7). He put his full weight on his money instead of on God, friends. I've seen what happens when you lean on something that can't hold you, like a cookie sheet with too many cookies on it.

The answer is False. The psalm says he "…strengthened himself by destruction." (Psalm 52:7). Helping others isn't anywhere in that line, friends. His strength came from destruction, not from helping anyone.

The answer is flourishing. David says, "But I am like an olive tree flourishing in the house of God…" (Psalm 52:8). A flourishing tree is green, healthy and growing, friends. After a verse about being uprooted, that's quite a picture to land on.

The answer is True. David says, "I trust in the loving devotion of God forever and ever." (Psalm 52:8). The mighty man leaned on his wealth, and David leans on God's loving devotion, friends. That's the whole difference, and it lasts forever and ever.

The answer is because God has done it. David says, "I will praise You forever, because You have done it." (Psalm 52:9). His reason is what God has done, friends, and the praise doesn't stop. David gives no end date.

The answer is in the presence of God's saints. David says he will wait on God's name, because it is good, "…in the presence of Your saints." (Psalm 52:9). Friends, he waits with God's people around him. I think waiting with company sounds a lot easier.
